title: Claude Fable 5, Mythos 5, and the Mythos-Class Tier
content:
## Overview

In June 2026, Anthropic introduced a new **"Mythos-class" tier** of models sitting above Opus in capability: **Claude Fable 5** (`claude-fable-5`), released broadly, and **Claude Mythos 5**, a more restricted sibling aimed at vetted cybersecurity partners. Days after launch, both were pulled from worldwide access for 19 days by a US government export-control order — then restored. The episode is one of the first cases of a frontier model being treated as a national-security export-control matter rather than purely a product-safety one.

---

## What Is the Mythos-Class Tier?

Anthropic describes Fable 5 as its most capable widely-released model, with state-of-the-art results on nearly all evaluated benchmarks. Key specs:

- **Always-on adaptive thinking** — the model applies extended reasoning automatically rather than as an opt-in mode
- **1M-token context window**, 128K max output tokens
- New safeguards designed to block responses in specific high-risk domains, including cybersecurity and biology, which Anthropic credits for making a broad release possible at all

Mythos 5 is a further-restricted variant made available only to trusted partners under Anthropic's **"Project Glasswing"** program, focused on cybersecurity use cases.

---

## Timeline: The June 2026 Shutdown

- **June 9, 2026** — Fable 5 launches for general users; Mythos 5 launches in parallel for Project Glasswing cybersecurity partners only.
- **June 12, 2026** — Amazon researchers report a jailbreak technique that bypassed one of Fable 5's cybersecurity safeguards; the finding is flagged to federal authorities by Amazon CEO Andy Jassy. The same day, the US government issues an export-control order requiring Anthropic to cut off access to both Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for any foreign national, anywhere — including Anthropic's own non-citizen employees. Because Anthropic had no reliable way to verify every user's nationality in real time, it shut down both models globally, for all users, effective immediately.
- **June 26, 2026** — The US government partially reverses course, authorizing Anthropic to restore Mythos 5 access to a set of trusted US organizations and federal agencies (roughly 100 companies/agencies).
- **June 30, 2026** — Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick sends a letter withdrawing the June 12 export-control license requirement for both models entirely.
- **July 1, 2026** — Fable 5 begins rolling out globally again across the Claude Platform, Claude.ai, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork (access via AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry follows shortly after). Mythos 5 remains limited to approved US organizations under continued Project Glasswing review, with Anthropic working with federal authorities to expand access further.

In total, the models were unavailable worldwide for about 19 days.

---

## Why the Ban Happened

The trigger wasn't a policy decision by Anthropic — it was an external jailbreak finding escalated through a competitor (Amazon) directly to federal authorities, which then produced an export-control order with no grace period. The order's scope (blocking *any* foreign national, including Anthropic's own staff) was broader than a typical content-safety patch could address, which is why Anthropic's response was a full shutdown rather than a targeted safeguard fix.

---

## Why It Matters

- **A new kind of availability risk.** Frontier models above a certain capability threshold can now be pulled from the market by export-control action, independent of the vendor's own safety assessment or customer contracts — a risk enterprises hadn't previously had to plan around.
- **"AI as infrastructure."** Commentators framed the 19-day shutdown as a wake-up call for any business that had already built production workflows on Fable 5 or Mythos 5 with no fallback model configured.
- **Precedent for future Mythos-class releases.** The episode establishes that models positioned above Opus may face a slower, government-reviewed rollout (as Mythos 5's continued restriction shows) even after the general-purpose sibling (Fable 5) is cleared.

See [Claude Model History](claude-model-history) for how Fable 5 and Mythos 5 fit into Anthropic's broader Claude 5 generation, alongside Sonnet 5 and Opus 4.8.
